# Vineyard Weather & Climate Intelligence — design brief

**Date:** 2026-07-25
**Status:** DESIGN — approved. 4A plan written: `docs/GIS/phases/phase-8-weather-climate-spine-plan.md`.
Runbook phases: **P8** = Release 4A (climate spine), **P9** = Release 4B (disease). NB "Phase 4"/"P4" is
soil, not weather — weather is Release 4 at the brief level but phases P8/P9 in the runbook map.
**Mode:** Builder / intrapreneurship (owner-developer)
**Generated by:** /office-hours
**Relates to:** `docs/GIS/vineyard-intelligence-discovery-brief.md` (§13 layer stack, §11.4 SSURGO snapshot pattern), VI P1/P2/P3

---

## 1. Problem statement

A winemaker cannot see weather the way they can now see vigor (NDVI). The nearest public weather
station is often kilometers away and hundreds of meters different in elevation, so its raw numbers do
not describe the vineyard. We want to show, per vineyard:

> "The nearest NOAA station (12 km away, 300 m lower) reads X. Our elevation-corrected model estimates
> your site at Y." — and turn that into the climate metrics a grower actually decides on: growing
> degree days, region classification, frost/heat risk, and disease pressure.

Weather is the missing **environmental driver** beneath everything VI already tracks: NDVI vigor, Brix
trajectory, phenology, and the IPM knowledge base. GDD + disease risk is what ties those together into
decision support instead of four disconnected charts.

## 2. The job (v1 scope, confirmed)

1. **Season climate & GDD tracking** — Growing Degree Days, Winkler index / Growing Season Temperature
   region classification, accumulation vs the site's own history ("8% ahead of your 10-year average"),
   harvest-timing context.
2. **Risk alerts** — spring/fall frost dates and events, heat-spike days, and disease pressure via
   temperature/rain/RH models (see §5).
3. **Site climate characterization** — a per-vineyard "climate terroir" report from long-term normals:
   region class, typical season shape, frost window, heat accumulation.

## 3. Confirmed premises (the honesty boundaries)

- **P1 — Gridded value, not our interpolation.** The "at your site" estimate is read from a terrain-aware
  gridded product; we do NOT hand-roll station IDW. Terrain correction is inherited from the grid. We
  display the nearest NOAA GHCN station and the elevation delta beside the estimate, for trust.
- **P2 — Site vs region, not block vs block.** One climate estimate per vineyard (planting-area
  centroid). All blocks in a vineyard share it in v1. Frost pockets, cold-air drainage, and aspect are
  **explicitly out of scope** — sub-km microclimate needs a physical downscaling model the free grids do
  not provide. The UI must say this so two identical block numbers are never read as "measured the same."
- **P3 — Disease models are screening indices, labeled "scout," never "diagnosis"** (product principle #7).
- **P4 — Reconstruct the diurnal curve from daily grids.** Disease indices want hourly data; grids are
  daily. We sine-interpolate hours-in-temperature-range from daily Tmin/Tmax. It is a *modeled* curve,
  caveated. Revisit in 4B only if botrytis/downy precision demands an hourly source.
- **P5 — SSURGO snapshot pattern, no geospatial worker.** Point extraction is a lightweight JSON fetch,
  so unlike NDVI this needs no worker. Tenant-scoped tables, dated per-vineyard snapshots populated by a
  cron sweep, rendered offline from storage. Provider abstraction: US-high-res + global fallback.

## 4. Data sources — a tiered provider registry selected by location

There is no single best source. The winning model is a **tiered registry**: for each vineyard we pick
the best available *primary* by location and data completeness, show the others as comparison, and use
grids as gap-fill. A grower can override the primary (they know their local station). Every number
carries its provenance. Adding a network is a plug-in against one `ClimateProvider` interface, not a
rewrite.

### 4.1 The tiers

**Tier 1 — regional ag mesonets (ag-sited, measure RH/solar/wind/ETo, grower-trusted).** Often the best
*primary* where present, because they carry the disease/irrigation variables bare NOAA COOP stations lack.

| Network | Coverage | API | Key? | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **CIMIS** | California | REST, JSON/XML, daily + hourly | **Yes** (free AppKey) | 150+ stations **+ Spatial CIMIS 2 km gridded** ETo/solar. Cleanest API. Carries ETo/RH/wind/solar/precip. |
| **AgriMet** (USBR) | Pacific NW + western US | URL/CSV web services | No | 300+ ag stations; 15-min → daily Tmax/Tmin/solar/wind/precip/ETr. Scriptable but crude (delimited text). |
| **NEWA** (Cornell/NRCC) | Northeast → Minnesota | CSV/tool; station data via **NRCC/ACIS** | Partnership for full API | **Already runs validated grape disease models** (black rot, Phomopsis, powdery mildew) + grape cold-hardiness. See §5.2 — a "don't reinvent" opportunity, at minimum a validation oracle. |

**Tier 2 — national stations (the "your nearest station" default everywhere in the US).**

| Source | Purpose | API | Key? | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **NOAA NCDC/CDO v2** (GHCN-Daily) | Historical + 1991–2020 normals | REST | **Yes** (free token) | The right well for history/normals. Laggy per-station for *live* data. |
| **RCC-ACIS** | Near-real-time station daily Tmax/Tmin/precip | REST | No | The pragmatic live-station feed climatologists actually use; better latency + station selection than CDO. Also backs NEWA. |

**Tier 3 — gridded, terrain-aware (gap-fill + area context + the "site estimate vs station").**

| Source | Role | Resolution / latency | Key? | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **gridMET** | **Primary live/in-season CONUS grid** | 4 km daily, **~14 h latency (near-real-time)** | No | Carries temp + precip + **RH + VPD + ref-ET** together. This is the in-season workhorse. |
| **Daymet** (NASA/ORNL) | **Historical baseline + finer 1 km spatial** | 1 km daily, **released annually (~3-month lag)**; monthly-latency product ~1 month behind | No | Great for "vs your 10-year average"; **too laggy to be the live source** — this is why gridMET is primary. |
| **Spatial CIMIS** | CA gridded ETo/solar | 2 km daily | Yes (AppKey) | Finer + ag-tuned for California; folds under the CIMIS provider. |

**Tier 4 — global fallback (non-US, e.g. Bhutan Wine Co).**

| Source | Resolution / coverage | Key? | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **NASA POWER** | ~0.5° (~50 km), global, agroclimate | No | Coherent "coarse global estimate" state, never "unavailable." Honest caveat: ~50 km in Himalayan terrain is rough for both temp and precip. |

**Everywhere — site elevation to explain the station gap.**

| Source | Purpose | Key? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **USGS EPQS** point elevation | Display the station-vs-site elevation delta; not used to compute the estimate | No |

Weather always has *some* fallback (unlike SSURGO, which was US-only-or-nothing) — non-US just drops to
a coarser tier. Label the active provider + resolution on every reading (the NDVI rule: "a legend without
its calibration mode is incomplete").

### 4.2 Multi-source model — primary + comparison + gap-fill, per metric, **spread not blend**

The grower's own instinct drives this: show every source side by side, let them pick who to trust.

- **One selected *primary* per vineyard** (default = best available Tier-1/Tier-2 station by distance,
  elevation delta, and completeness). Grids and other stations shown as **comparison context**.
- **Gap-fill, not blend:** when the primary is missing days, backfill from the live grid and *stamp the
  fill* ("GDD from Sonoma Co. Airport, 3 days backfilled from gridMET").
- **Per-metric sourcing is forced, not optional.** Most COOP stations report only Tmax/Tmin/PRCP/SNOW —
  no humidity. So: temp/GDD/frost from the trusted station; precip from a *close* station (grids are weak
  on daily precip) else the grid; **RH/VPD must come from gridMET / CIMIS / POWER** because the station
  can't measure it. Make the per-metric source visible.
- **Never silently average.** Averaging is a trap: (1) the station is an *input* to Daymet/gridMET, so
  they're not independent — averaging double-counts it; (2) a point and a 1–50 km area average don't
  combine into a better point; (3) blending drags the good precip number toward the fuzzy one; (4) GDD is
  an accumulator and latency makes a day-varying blend un-reproducible. If we ever offer an ensemble, show
  the **spread** ("sources range 1,190–1,240, agreement good") — wide disagreement is a *signal to trust
  the map less*, and a hidden average throws that signal away.
- **Provenance on every number and every derived metric** (which source, which days filled, computed how).

### 4.3 Accuracy — temperature good, precipitation is the weak link (and it's the disease input)

- **Temperature is the strong variable.** Daymet cross-validation: `Tmax` MAE ≈ **1.2–1.8 °C**, `Tmin`
  somewhat worse (inversions, cold-air pooling). gridMET is comparable (inherits PRISM climatology).
  Elevation constrains temperature through lapse rates, so grids interpolate temp well between stations.
- **Precipitation fails in two ways** — *did it rain* (usually right) and *how much* (often off). Seasonal
  and monthly totals track well; individual **daily** amounts in convective/complex terrain carry large
  relative error. No free grid fixes this — it's physics. The single best precip fix is a **$150 on-site
  rain gauge** (see §9, "Later"), which also gives per-tenant ground truth to validate the grid against.
- **Decision implications:** GDD/Winkler trends and "vs your own history" are trustworthy, but near a
  **Winkler region-class boundary** show the number, not just the class. **Frost** = temp error (~2 °C
  `Tmin`) *stacked on* the P2 spatial limit → always "elevated risk, go check," never "you're safe."
  **Downy/botrytis** lean on the least-reliable variable (daily precip) → a second reason (on top of P3)
  they stay *screening*, never diagnosis.

## 5. Metrics & models

### 5.1 Climate (4A — daily grids, no diurnal reconstruction needed)
- **GDD** — base 10 °C, `max(0, (Tmax+Tmin)/2 − 10)`, with a configurable upper cap (Winkler uses none;
  offer a 30 °C cap toggle). Accumulate over the growing season; compare to the site's own prior years.
- **Winkler index / regions I–V** — Apr 1–Oct 31 GDD sum → region class.
- **Growing Season Temperature (GST)** — Apr–Oct mean temp → Jones climate-maturity grouping.
- **Frost** — last spring frost / first fall frost dates; frost events below configurable thresholds
  (0 °C, −2 °C). Honesty note: grid daily-min at 1–4 km will miss a frost pocket (P2).
- **Heat** — count of days above configurable thresholds (30/35/38 °C); heat-spike flags.
- **Rainfall** — season accumulation, dry/wet spells (feeds downy + irrigation context).

### 5.2 Disease (4B — screening indices, diurnal reconstructed from daily Tmin/Tmax)
- **Powdery mildew → Gubler-Thomas (UC Davis) Risk Index.** Temperature-only, NO leaf wetness required.
  Risk points accrue on consecutive days with ≥6 continuous hours in 21–30 °C; heat >35 °C knocks points
  down. The clean one — a real California-viticulture standard. Hours-in-range come from the reconstructed
  diurnal curve.
- **Downy mildew → "3-10 rule" proxy.** Temp ≥10 °C + ~10 mm rain over 24–48 h + shoots ~10 cm. Rain is
  in the grid; a defensible screening heuristic. The sensor-grade models (DMCast) need leaf wetness we do
  not have — say so.
- **Botrytis → temp + RH + rain proxy (bloom + pre-harvest windows).** The weakest without wetness
  duration; heaviest caveats. gridMET RH feeds it. Frame strictly as "scout the fruit zone," not a call.

Every disease output is a *risk index that prompts scouting*, cross-linked to the IPM knowledge base.
Never a diagnosis. This is the highest-honesty-risk part of the feature; the copy matters as much as the
math.

**Don't reinvent for the Northeast — NEWA already ships validated grape disease models** (black rot,
Phomopsis, powdery mildew) + grape cold-hardiness, run by Cornell/NRCC on ag-sited stations. For NE
tenants, prefer surfacing/validating against NEWA's models over running our own reconstructed-diurnal
index (Layer-1 "tried and true" beats a home-rolled proxy). At minimum NEWA is a **validation oracle** for
our Gubler-Thomas output. Full data-API access may require a partnership conversation with NEWA; the
underlying station data is reachable via NRCC/ACIS regardless.

## 6. Architecture (mirrors SSURGO §11.4, no worker)

```
Vineyard (planting-area centroid)
  → scheduled sweep (cron) → climate provider(s) [Daymet | gridMET | POWER] + GHCN nearest station + EPQS elevation
  → dated snapshot rows (tenant-scoped, RLS) in Postgres
  → console renders OFFLINE from stored snapshot (no live call on page open)
```

- **No geospatial worker.** JSON point-extraction only. Preserves the VI no-worker hypothesis (unlike the
  NDVI raster path). This is the load-bearing architectural win of choosing gridded-point over raster.
- **Snapshot + provenance**, not live-on-open: store provider, resolution, grid-cell coords, station id +
  distance + elevation delta, pull date, and a source fingerprint (like the SSURGO polygon fingerprint) so
  a snapshot can be marked stale and superseded without losing history.
- **Provider abstraction (the load-bearing design)** — one `ClimateProvider` interface; the tiered
  registry of §4 is a set of plug-in implementations selected by vineyard location + completeness.
  **Build the abstraction first, integrate networks incrementally.** Seven live integrations before
  shipping anything is an ocean, not a lake: v1 (4A) ships with ACIS/CDO stations + gridMET + POWER, then
  add CIMIS / AgriMet / NEWA as provider plug-ins prioritized by *where the tenant's vineyards actually
  are* (CA → CIMIS first; NE → NEWA first; PNW → AgriMet first). Each added network must `log()` its
  coverage so a gap never reads as "covered."
- **Pure metric modules** — GDD/Winkler/GST/frost/heat/diurnal-reconstruction/disease-index math lives in
  `src/lib/weather/*` as pure, unit-tested functions independent of React/Leaflet/Prisma (same discipline
  as the NDVI `render.ts`/`color.ts` split).

### 6.1 Provisional tables (all follow the Phase-12 tenant checklist: `tenantId`, `@@index`, FK→organization, RLS FORCE + policy, app_rls grants, isolation test)
- `VineyardWeatherSnapshot` — one dated pull per vineyard: provider, resolution, cell coords, station ref,
  elevation delta, fingerprint, status (current/superseded/stale).
- `VineyardClimateMetric` / daily series — the extracted daily values + derived GDD/frost/heat, keyed to a
  snapshot; enough to recompute season aggregates and disease indices offline.
- `WeatherProviderUsage` — request/quota counter per provider (CDO has a 10k/day, 5 req/s cap), mirroring
  the `cdse_usage_counter` pattern from NDVI.

Does NOT touch ledger / cost / compliance / commerce — no data-model-coalescence parity concern. This is
VI/moat-adjacent, additive.

## 7. Assistant coverage (definition of done — `verify:ai-native`)
A new `*-core.ts` fails `verify:ai-native` until it has a tool + golden eval. Ship at least:
- `query_climate` — "what's my GDD vs last year", "what Winkler region is Russian River Ranch", "when was
  last spring frost".
- `query_disease_risk` — "powdery risk this week", "is downy pressure building".
These are read/query tools (no writes), so no confirmation-card path needed. One domain-composite tool per
concern, not one per micro-metric (per the assistant STOP-rule / ~40-tool ceiling in memory).

Fold the **alert engine** in here too (Approach C's good idea, not a separate path): frost/heat/disease
threshold crossings emit to the existing inbox/notification surface.

## 8. Distribution
A new console area under `/vineyards` ("Weather & Climate" / "Climate Intelligence"), reusing existing
chart patterns (`BrixChart`, `AnalyteTrendChart`, `src/lib/harvest/chart.ts`) and the discovery-brief map
layer-stack contract (§13.1) for an optional map overlay of the site estimate. No new runtime deps for the
data path (raw fetch + JSON).

## 9. Release slicing (Approach A)

### Release 4A — climate spine
- Provider abstraction + Daymet/gridMET/POWER point extraction + GHCN nearest-station + EPQS elevation.
- Snapshot tables (tenant checklist) + cron sweep + quota counter.
- GDD / Winkler / GST / frost / heat / rainfall pure modules + tests.
- Console: per-vineyard climate card, season GDD chart vs prior years, site-characterization report,
  station-vs-estimate + elevation-delta panel.
- `query_climate` assistant tool + golden eval. Frost/heat alert to inbox.

### Release 4B — disease intelligence
- Diurnal reconstruction module (sine, from daily Tmin/Tmax) + tests.
- Gubler-Thomas powdery, 3-10 downy proxy, botrytis temp+RH+rain proxy — each a pure indexed module,
  each cross-linked to the IPM KB, each labeled "scout not diagnose."
- `query_disease_risk` tool + golden eval. Disease-pressure alert to inbox.
- Decision gate: if reconstructed-diurnal proves too coarse for botrytis/downy, spike ERA5-Land/Open-Meteo
  hourly for the disease slice only (keep daily grids for climate).

### Later
- **On-site sensor ingestion** — a grower's own weather station / rain gauge (Onset, KestrelMet, Davis,
  or a cheap tipping-bucket) as a Tier-0 primary. Fixes the daily-precip weak link at the source, ingests
  into the discovery-brief observation model (§9.2), and becomes per-tenant ground truth to validate every
  grid against. Highest-value "later" for anyone precip-driven-disease serious.
- **NEWA model integration (NE)** — beyond validation, surface NEWA's grape disease + cold-hardiness
  outputs directly for Northeast tenants (partnership permitting).
- Physical sub-km downscaling (lapse-rate + cold-air-pooling + aspect) to lift the P2 boundary → true
  block-level microclimate & frost-pocket mapping. The research-grade sequel, not v1.
- Forecast integration (NWS api.weather.gov) for forward-looking alerts vs the current historical/estimate.
- ET / irrigation scheduling (gridMET / CIMIS / AgriMet ref-ET already pulled).

## 10. Open questions
- **Which providers ship in 4A** — recommend ACIS/CDO stations + gridMET (live) + POWER (global) at launch;
  CIMIS/AgriMet/NEWA added as plug-ins by tenant geography (§6.1). Confirm against where the real early
  tenants sit.
- **Primary-selection heuristic** — how we auto-pick the default primary per vineyard (station distance,
  elevation delta, % complete days) before the grower overrides. Needs a concrete rule + a "why this
  source" explainer in the UI.
- **API keys / env** — CIMIS AppKey + NOAA CDO token are per-provider secrets; NEWA full API may need a
  partnership. One `WeatherProviderUsage` quota counter per provider (CDO caps at 10k/day, 5 req/s).
- **ACIS vs CDO split** — CDO for history/normals, ACIS for near-real-time station daily. Confirm ACIS
  station coverage/latency in the spike.
- **GDD base/cap defaults** — base 10 °C standard; expose the upper cap (30 °C toggle) per vineyard.
- **Snapshot cadence** — likely a daily append + weekly recompute of season aggregates. Disease wants
  daily; climate can be looser.

## 11. Success criteria
- A grower opens a vineyard and sees: current-season GDD vs their own history, Winkler/GST region, frost &
  heat counts, and (4B) a powdery/downy/botrytis risk index — each with the nearest station, the elevation
  delta, the provider + resolution, and a "scout, don't diagnose" honesty line.
- **Multi-source is visible, not hidden:** the primary source is grower-selectable per vineyard, other
  sources show as comparison, gap-fills are stamped, and any ensemble shows **spread, never a blended
  single value**. Every number and derived metric carries its provenance.
- **Honesty lines render, not just exist:** Winkler shows the number at region-class boundaries; frost is
  always "elevated risk → check," never "safe"; daily precip is flagged as the low-confidence variable.
- Non-US tenant (Bhutan) gets a coherent coarse-global estimate, never a blank.
- `verify:ai-native` green (tools + goldens exist). Tenant-isolation test covers every new table.
- No geospatial worker introduced.

## 12. The assignment
Before `/plan`: **register a free NOAA CDO token + a free CIMIS AppKey**, then do a ~45-minute spike
hitting, for *one real vineyard's* lat/lon (Russian River Ranch **and** Bhutan): **gridMET** (live),
**Daymet** single-pixel (historical), **NASA POWER** (global), **CIMIS** station + Spatial CIMIS (CA),
**RCC-ACIS** nearest-station daily, plus GHCN normals + EPQS elevation. Confirm the JSON/CSV shapes, the
real latency of each, that a CA vineyard gets a *dense* CIMIS/ACIS station and Bhutan actually returns
from POWER. That single spike de-risks P1, P5, and the whole tiered-registry bet — everything rides on
those point APIs behaving and on the per-vineyard "best primary" actually being pickable. The rest is math
you already know how to write.

## 13. What I noticed about how you think
- You reached for "map it spatially... this is what we *think* it was at your vineyard" — you instinctively
  wanted the honest gap between the measurement and the estimate, which is exactly the trust move. You
  didn't have the word "gridded reanalysis," but you'd already described its job.
- You immediately named the specific disease models — "powdery mildew index... downy... botrytis... in
  such a way that doesn't require leaf wetness." That last clause is the whole engineering constraint, and
  you stated it before I did. That's domain knowledge doing the scoping for you.
- You accepted P2 (no per-block microclimate in v1) without flinching. A lot of people want the map to
  promise more than the data can see; you took the honest boundary. That instinct is what keeps this
  feature from lying to your own customers.
```
